analyst_view.overall: Strasbourg (13th, 10 points, five defeats in six) sacked Hugo Oliveira on Wednesday evening and appointed Vítor Matos from Swansea, who starts with this home game after barely two days with the squad. Brest (9th, 15 points) arrive in form after wins at Lorient and 2-0 against Lyon. Strasbourg have the fourth-best attack but the 16th defence; Panichelli is out and Fabio Baldé, goalkeeper Jørgensen and Reyna are doubts, while Brest miss Chardonnet and Le Guen with Sa. Diop doubtful, mostly already in the numbers. Azzedine Souifi referees; the numbers know only four of his top-flight games and blend them with an average record.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, a high figure driven by Strasbourg's open games. A coach who has just arrived usually starts by trying to stop the bleeding at the back, so I lean slightly lower, to about 3.2; Panichelli's absence is already counted.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners. I found nothing about Matos changing the shape at once (both teams are expected in a 4-3-3), so I stay at 8.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards. Souifi has only four games in the numbers, which already blend his record with an average referee, and I found nothing that suggests a heated game, so I stay at 3.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots. A new-coach lift at home could add some energy, but a more cautious setup takes some away, so I stay at 24.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. With Strasbourg likely to be more careful under a coach in his first game and their main striker Panichelli out, I trim slightly to about 8.6.
